title: AnA: An Attentive Autonomous Driving System
problem: Current autonomous driving perception modules execute unconditionally and uniformly regardless of driving context, wasting compute on irrelevant scenes and missing safety-critical events that require focused attention—a mismatch from how humans selectively allocate perception resources.
motivation: Compute resources on autonomous vehicles are limited and latency-sensitive; a system that directs perception effort toward driving-relevant objects and events can reduce unnecessary computation while improving safety response time.
method: AnA inserts three components between planning and perception: a query interface where the planner requests specific perception tasks based on driving context, a query executor that selects which tasks to run, and a monitor that catches execution problems. Rather than analyzing every scene uniformly, the system switches between a fast, broad scan and a detailed analysis of safety-critical elements, mirroring how human drivers focus attention where it matters most.
key_novelty: The system empowers the driving planner to selectively activate perception tasks based on driving context, reducing unnecessary computation by 44% while cutting collisions in half on adversarial benchmarks.
contributions: Query interface enabling the planning module to direct perception with driving-context knowledge.
Query executor that selects the optimal perception task subset given planner queries.
Anomaly monitor integrating driving knowledge to handle unexpected perception outcomes.
Empirical demonstration of 2x collision reduction and 44% compute savings on challenging ADS benchmarks.

metrics.speedup: 44% compute reduction without compromising driving safety
metrics.other: 2x reduction in collisions on adversarial events

limitations: Not discussed; performance under distribution-shifted or adversarial sensor inputs beyond the test benchmarks is unclear.
primary_theme: Query-driven attentive perception scheduling for autonomous driving
